daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo issued an ultimatum to regional heads, warning he would not hesitate to intervene directly in their affairs. In separate remarks, Prabowo reaffirmed his commitment to empowering vulnerable communities. The president also criticized the small font size in school textbooks and announced the government would undertake educational reforms.

  • The Attorney General's Office will appoint an investigation team to handle two pretrial lawsuits filed by money laundering suspect Febrie Adriansyah, who was examined for seven hours and faced more than 20 questions during interrogation.
  • A DPR member questioned the purpose of 995 firearms and drugs found at a South Jakarta school, calling for a thorough investigation into the matter.
  • Commission III of the DPR denied rumors of a presidential letter regarding the replacement of the National Police Chief, urging an end to speculation.
  • A labor coalition announced that August demonstrations have only been postponed, not canceled.
  • Constitutional Court Justice Saldi Isra warned that changes to transfer payments threaten regional PPPK budgets, with local governments protesting the impact.
  • Two people were arrested for uploading and commenting on Prabowo's speech about Iran's nuclear program, prompting Kompolnas to remind authorities of a Constitutional Court ruling that digital disruptions are not criminal offenses.
  • The Ministry of Law formed a team to expedite construction of permanent Sekolah Rakyat buildings.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia began constructing a Scorpene submarine for the Navy, marking a significant milestone in the country's defence modernization efforts. This development represents a major advancement in Indonesia's naval capabilities and domestic shipbuilding industry.

  • Indonesia and Japan agreed to cooperate on developing railway signaling technology, strengthening bilateral technical collaboration.
  • The Indonesian Consulate General showcased Indonesian arts and culture aboard the Royal Kuching Cruise in Malaysia.
  • Indonesia will assess damage from the Montara oil spill in East Nusa Tenggara.

Other

A major fire engulfed the DKI Jakarta Bapenda building, with 20 fire units deployed to fight the blaze that engulfed floors 11 through 16. One victim was evacuated from the 15th floor, and Polri's forensic laboratory was deployed to investigate the cause.

  • Bank Indonesia linked US$3.8 billion worth of Kalimantan projects with potential investors to boost regional development.
  • The National Disaster Management Agency confirmed that wildfires across four provinces have been brought under control, while deploying additional helicopters to fight fires in West Kalimantan.
  • The government announced that AI Factory strengthens Indonesia's position as a regional artificial intelligence hub.
  • Police seized 996 guns from a South Jakarta school, while Bali Customs foiled a 10.1 kg marijuana smuggling attempt.
  • BPOM closed a factory and named an employee as suspect after MinyaKita cooking oil was found to smell like diesel fuel.
